process.text: class="flex-1"> How We Work Our Process Six steps, the same on every roof — from the first photograph on the deck to the warranty in your hand. Documented, unhurried, and checked at every stage. Our Process · Step by Step 01 Inspection Free, thorough, documented. We get on the roof and into the attic, photograph what we find, and walk you through it — deck, flashing, ventilation, everything. You keep the photos either way. Deck inspection — Murray, UT Storm Damage & Insurance We document. You decide. If the inspection turns up hail or wind damage, we record it the way insurance claims require — dated photos, measurements, and a written scope. The claim is yours to file; the documentation comes from us. 02 Estimate A written scope with system options and real numbers. Take it home, compare it, sleep on it. No pressure, and no expiring “today only” pricing. 03 Materials Your system, color, and components confirmed — surface, underlayment, flashing, ventilation — then ordered and staged so install day starts at the deck, not at the supply house. Install day — staging 04 Installation Most residential roofs take one to two days. The deck is repaired and dried in first, then every layer goes down in order per The Installer's Standard — and every course is checked before the next one starts. Underlayment dried in — Sandy, UT 05 Walkthrough We inspect the finished roof together. Flashing, ridge lines, cleanup, the magnetic nail sweep — nothing is done until it's right, and you've seen it yourself. 06 Warranty A manufacturer warranty on the system and a workmanship warranty on the install — both in writing, both explained before we leave the driveway. The Installer’s Standard Six principles, Every roof Every step above is measured against the six principles we install by. They’re not a slogan — they’re the checklist on the roof. 01 / Preparation The deck is inspected and repaired before anything goes down on it. 02 / Flashing New metal at every wall, valley, and penetration — never reused, never caulked over. 03 / Ventilation Intake and exhaust balanced to the attic, not to the brochure. 04 / Layering Each course overlaps the one below it, the way water expects. 05 / Precision Straight lines, correct nail placement, manufacturer specs on every course. 06 / Clean Site Tarped landscaping, daily pickup, and a magnetic sweep before we leave. services_roof_replacement.text: class="flex-1"> Our Services Services / Roof Replacement Roof Replacement A new roof is a system, not just shingles. We build the whole thing. Roof Replacement — Salt Lake Valley The Service How we approach it When a roof reaches the end of its life, the answer is a complete system — not a cover-up. We tear off down to the deck, repair what the old roof was hiding, and rebuild every layer: ice and water shield at the eaves and valleys, synthetic underlayment, new flashing, balanced ventilation, and the surface you choose — architectural shingle, metal, or tile. Built for the Salt Lake Valley's snow loads, freeze-thaw cycles, and high-altitude sun. Get a Free Estimate Ice & water shield at the eaves The Difference Why it's done this way 01 Full tear-off, every time We remove the old roof completely instead of layering over it, so deck damage gets found and fixed — not buried. 02 Built for Utah winters Ice and water shield at eaves and valleys stops ice-dam backup, and the system is specified for valley snow loads. 03 Ventilation done right Balanced intake and exhaust extends shingle life, reduces attic heat in summer, and helps prevent ice dams in winter. 04 Material options that fit Architectural shingle, standing seam metal, or tile — we walk you through lifespan, look, and cost so the choice is yours. System No. 01 The Classic Architectural Asphalt Shingle 25–50 years depending on product class Entry — High End System No. 02 The Standing Seam Metal Roofing 50–70 years with proper coating maintenance Premium System No. 03 The Heritage Clay & Concrete Tile 50 years (concrete) to lifetime (clay) Mid — High End Explore Roofing Systems FAQs Common questions How do I know if I need a replacement instead of a repair? + Age, widespread granule loss, curling or brittle shingles, and repeated leaks in different spots all point to replacement. If a repair will genuinely solve it, we'll tell you that instead — the free inspection is where we sort this out honestly. How long does a roof replacement take? + Most residential replacements take one to three days once work begins, depending on roof size, pitch, and material. Weather can shift the schedule, and we won't open more roof than we can dry-in the same day. What drives the cost of a new roof? + Roof size and pitch, material choice, the amount of deck repair needed, and details like chimneys, valleys, and skylights. Will insurance cover my roof replacement? + If the damage is from a covered event like hail or wind, it may. We document the damage thoroughly, provide the reports your adjuster needs, and can meet the adjuster on-site — but the claim decision is always your insurer's. services_roof_repair.text: class="flex-1"> Our Services Services / Roof Repair Roof Repair Find the real source. Fix it once. That's the whole job. Roof Repair — Salt Lake Valley The Service How we approach it Most roof leaks don't start where the water shows up. We diagnose first — tracing the leak to its actual source before anything gets touched — then repair it properly. Wind-lifted shingles off the canyon gusts, flashing failures around chimneys and vents, summer hail damage, ice-dam wear at the eaves: the Salt Lake Valley throws all of it at a roof, and we fix all of it. Get a Free Estimate Step flashing at the chimney line The Difference Why it's done this way 01 Diagnosis before repair We trace the leak to its source instead of patching where the stain appears, so the same problem doesn't come back next storm. 02 Stops small problems early A lifted shingle or failed pipe boot costs little to fix now and a lot to fix after a season of water intrusion. 03 Extends your roof's life Timely, correct repairs add years to a roof that doesn't need replacing yet — and we'll tell you honestly when it does. 04 Storm-response experience Canyon winds and summer hail are routine here. We know what they do to a roof and how to document it for insurance. Scope of Work What's included 01 Leak tracing We follow the water to its entry point — attic, deck, flashing — before quoting the fix. 02 Shingle repair & replacement Wind-lifted, cracked, or missing shingles replaced and sealed, matched as closely as possible. 03 Flashing repair Chimney, valley, step, and vent flashing resealed or replaced — the most common leak source on valley homes. 04 Pipe boot & vent replacement Cracked rubber boots and damaged vents swapped before they let water in. 05 Hail & wind damage repair Storm damage repaired and documented with photos suitable for an insurance claim. 06 Ice-dam damage repair Eave and gutter-line damage from winter ice backup repaired, with prevention recommendations. 07 Repair report & photos Before-and-after photos and a written summary of what was wrong and what we did. Why does my roof only leak during certain storms? + Wind direction, rain intensity, and snowmelt each stress different parts of the roof. A flashing gap might only leak in wind-driven rain from the south; ice dams only show up in freeze-thaw weather. This is exactly why we diagnose before we repair. Is it worth repairing an older roof, or should I just replace it? + It depends on the roof's overall condition, not just its age. If the system is sound and the damage is localized, a repair is the right call. If failures are spreading, we'll show you why replacement is the better investment — with photos, not pressure. Can hail damage be invisible from the ground? + Yes. Hail bruises shingles and knocks off granules in ways you often can't see from the driveway, but that shorten the roof's life. After a hailstorm it's worth a free inspection — and if there's claimable damage, we document it properly. Do you repair roofs in winter? + Yes. Leaks don't wait for spring, and neither do we. We work in dry weather windows and use cold-rated materials and methods so winter repairs hold just as well. We install TPO and EPDM membrane systems engineered for it: heat-welded seams that form a monolithic surface, proper drainage detailing, and water testing before we sign off. services_solar_detach_reset.text: class="flex-1"> Our Services Services / Solar Detach & Reset Solar Detach & Reset Re-roofing under solar panels, without putting either warranty at risk. Solar Detach & Reset — Salt Lake Valley The Service How we approach it Thousands of Salt Lake Valley homes now have solar — and every one of those roofs will eventually need replacement. A detach and reset is the right way to do it: panels and racking removed, the roof rebuilt as a complete system, mounts properly flashed into the new roof, and the array reinstalled — all coordinated with your solar installer so both your roofing warranty and your solar warranty come through intact. Get a Free Estimate Mounts flashed into the new roof The Difference Why it's done this way 01 Both warranties protected We coordinate the solar work with qualified installers so the panel warranty survives, and we build the roof so its warranty does too. 02 One coordinated project We manage the sequence — detach, re-roof, reset — so you're not playing scheduler between a roofer and a solar company. 03 Mounts flashed correctly Every roof penetration for racking gets properly flashed and sealed into the new system. Mount points are where solar roofs leak. 04 No corners cut around the array The roof under and around the panels gets the same full system — membrane, underlayment, flashing — as the rest of the roof. Scope of Work What's included 01 Pre-project documentation The array's layout, wiring, and condition documented before a single panel moves. 02 Solar installer coordination We work with your original installer or a qualified solar partner for the electrical detach and reset. 03 Panel & racking removal Panels and rails removed and stored safely on-site or off, protected for the duration. 04 Full roof replacement Complete tear-off and system rebuild underneath — deck repair, membrane, underlayment, flashing, ventilation. 05 Mount flashing & sealing Racking attachment points flashed into the new roof system, not just caulked over. 06 Panel reinstallation Array reset to its engineered layout, torqued and aligned to spec. 07 System verification Solar production confirmed operational and the roof walked with you at completion. The Process How the work runs Scope and price are set in a written estimate before any work begins — no surprises once the job is underway. 01 Inspection — roof condition and array documentation 02 Coordination — schedule aligned with the solar installer 03 Detach — panels and racking removed and protected 04 Re-roof — full system rebuild, deck to surface 05 Mount integration — attachment points flashed into the new roof 06 Reset — array reinstalled to its original engineered layout 07 Verification — solar output confirmed, final walkthrough Array reset to its engineered layout FAQs Common questions Why can't you just roof around the panels? + Because the roof under the array ages like the rest of it, and leaving it means a guaranteed leak under thousands of dollars of equipment. A partial roof around solar also creates seams and transitions that fail. The full detach and reset costs more up front and is the only version worth doing. Will removing my panels void the solar warranty? + Not when it's done right. Warranties generally require qualified personnel for detach and reset work, which is exactly why we coordinate with your original installer or a qualified solar partner rather than moving panels ourselves. How much does a detach and reset add to a re-roof? + It depends on the array size, racking type, and whether your original installer handles the reset. We include the detach and reset as a clear line item in the free estimate so you can see the full picture before deciding. How long will my solar be offline? + Typically only the working days of the project — panels come down as the roof work starts and go back up when it's finished. For most homes that's a matter of days, and we sequence the work to keep the offline window as short as possible. My solar company is out of business — can you still do this? + Yes. It's increasingly common. We work with qualified solar partners who can handle the detach, reset, and system verification when the original installer is no longer around. Metal Roofing — Salt Lake Valley The Service How we approach it Metal is the long-game roof. Standing seam panels with concealed fasteners, or metal shake with a traditional profile — both engineered for 50 to 70 years of service. In the Salt Lake Valley that performance is practical, not theoretical: snow sheds instead of accumulating into ice dams, canyon winds meet interlocked panels instead of liftable shingles, and a Class A fire-rated surface stands between your home and ember exposure near the benches. Get a Free Estimate Concealed-fastener seam detail The Difference Why it's done this way 01 50–70 year service life A properly installed metal roof outlasts two to three asphalt roofs — often the last roof the house ever needs. 02 Snow and ice performance Smooth panels shed snow rather than holding it, reducing both snow load and the ice-dam formation that plagues valley eaves. 03 Wind and fire resistance Interlocked, mechanically seamed panels resist canyon-wind uplift, and metal carries a Class A fire rating. 04 Looks that fit the home Crisp standing seam lines for modern homes, metal shake profiles for traditional ones — in a real range of finishes and colors. Scope of Work What's included 01 System & profile consultation Standing seam or metal shake, panel profile, gauge, and finish — chosen for your home and budget. 02 Complete tear-off & deck prep Old roofing removed, decking inspected and repaired, the substrate made right. 03 High-temp underlayment Synthetic underlayment rated for metal's heat and the valley's temperature swings. 04 Ice & water shield Self-sealing membrane at eaves and valleys — metal sheds snow, but the membrane backstops what melts. 05 Concealed-fastener installation Standing seam panels attached with hidden clips, so no exposed fasteners weather and loosen over time. 06 Trim, flashing & snow management Ridge, valley, and edge detailing in matching metal, with snow guards where shedding needs control. 07 Final inspection & walkthrough Seams, fasteners, and details verified, the site cleaned, and the finished roof reviewed with you. The Process How the work runs Scope and price are set in a written estimate before any work begins — no surprises once the job is underway. 01 Consultation — profiles, finishes, and an honest cost comparison 02 Free estimate — measured, itemized, no obligation 03 Material order — panels fabricated to your roof's dimensions 04 Tear-off & deck prep — clean substrate, repairs done 05 Underlayment & membrane — high-temp synthetic plus ice barrier 06 Panel installation — concealed fasteners, seamed and detailed 07 Inspection & walkthrough — verified, cleaned, reviewed together Panels fabricated to the roof's dimensions Roofing Systems · From the Brand Book The systems we install Each signature system has its own materials, lifespan, and available palette. A metal roof costs more than asphalt up front but lasts two to three times as long, with less maintenance along the way. We'll lay out both numbers in the estimate so you can decide on the full picture, not just the first price. Is metal noisy when it rains? + Not on a modern installation. Solid decking, underlayment, and attic insulation sit between the panels and your living space — over that assembly, rain on metal sounds about the same as rain on any roof. Standing seam or metal shake — what's the difference? + Standing seam is the clean, vertical-line profile with concealed fasteners — the premium modern look. Metal shake mimics the texture of traditional shake or shingle in metal, which suits homes where the classic profile fits better. Performance is comparable; the choice is mostly architectural. How does metal handle Utah snow and hail? + Well. Panels shed snow instead of holding it, which reduces ice-dam risk at the eaves, and we add snow guards over entries and walkways to control the release. Metal resists hail puncture better than asphalt, though severe hail can cosmetically dent panels — something insurance policies treat differently, and worth reviewing on yours. Can a metal roof go over my existing shingles? + It's sometimes done, but we recommend tear-off. Removing the old roof lets us inspect and repair the deck, install the right underlayment, and start the 50-plus-year system on a sound foundation — covering up an unknown deck undermines the whole point of buying longevity.
